title: The Artin-Schreier type polynomial P(z) obtained from a primitive pth root of unity has coefficients in the ideal generated by w = 1 - zeta and satisfies an addition formula

standard_prerequisites.name: The ring of integers Z[zeta] of a cyclotomic field and its unique prime above p
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: the reduction at proof lines 34992-34995 and the prime-ideal statement at proof lines 35003-35005
standard_prerequisites.use: Supplies the unique prime (w) above p and hence the relation p = u w^{p-1} that drives the computation of the coefficients a_i.

standard_prerequisites.name: Divisibility of cyclotomic polynomials and the identity p = prod_j (1 - zeta^j)
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: the factorization and its evaluation at t = 1 at proof lines 34996-35002
standard_prerequisites.use: Is the arithmetic input that identifies the valuation of p at w as p - 1.

core_obligations: Reduce the assertion to the universal case A = Z[zeta] = Z[x]/(x^{p-1} + ... + x + 1), the ring of integers of the cyclotomic field (proof lines 34992-34995).
Use the factorization t^{p-1} + ... + t + 1 = (t - zeta)...(t - zeta^{p-1}) and evaluate at t = 1 to get p = (1 - zeta)(1 - zeta^2)...(1 - zeta^{p-1}) (proof lines 34996-35002).

Identify (p, w) = (w) as the unique prime ideal of A above p, since a field of characteristic p has no nontrivial p-th root of unity, and conclude p = u w^{p-1} for a unit u (proof lines 35003-35005).

Deduce the explicit form a_i = (1/p) * binom(p, i) * u * w^{i-1} for p > i > 1, then use P(-1) = 0 to show a_1 lies in (w), finishing the first part; the second (addition) formula is stated to follow from a direct computation the author omits (proof lines 35008-35013).
difficulty_reason: The statement fixes a ring A containing a primitive p-th root of unity zeta, sets w = 1 - zeta, and asserts two things about P(z) = ((1 + wz)^p - 1)/w^p: that it has the shape z^p - z + sum a_i z^i with all a_i in the ideal (w), and that it satisfies the addition formula P(z_1 + z_2 + w z_1 z_2) = P(z_1) + P(z_2) + w^p P(z_1)P(z_2) (source lines 34976-34989). The proof must first reduce to the cyclotomic integer ring Z[zeta] (proof lines 34992-34995), then use the factorization of t^{p-1} + ... + t + 1 into the factors (t - zeta^j) and the evaluation t = 1 to obtain p = (1 - zeta)...(1 - zeta^{p-1}) (proof lines 34996-35002). The substantive step is recognising that (p, w) = (w) is the unique prime above p, which forces p = u w^{p-1} for a unit u and yields the explicit formula for the a_i (proof lines 35003-35011); the addition formula is then left to a direct computation the author omits.
